rows.description: A child is certain he knows the answer or can win the race and is stunned when wrong. His confidence is louder than his knowledge.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager says the syllabus is easy and skips revision, or thinks he can drive well after two tries. Ease of recognising material is mistaken for ability to recall it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult is very sure a plan, relationship or investment will work out and leaves no margin for error. Being wrong hurts more because doubt was never allowed in.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A team sees a peer promise fast delivery with total assurance. Wise leads ask for a range and a worst case rather than punishing or blindly trusting the certainty.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A grounded professional writes down predictions with percentages, checks them later, and learns where her sure feelings were reliable and where they were not.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager after a few videos on a subject believes he understands it better than his teacher. He does not yet know enough to see what he is missing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student who has just learned a framework feels like an expert until harder problems appear, and confidence drops before real skill grows. The dip is normal and useful.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A skilled young engineer assumes what is easy for her is easy for everyone and doubts her ability. Real skill can bring more awareness of gaps and less bragging.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A mentor gives specific examples and asks the newcomer to explain a task step by step so gaps show for themselves. Blunt ridicule only hardens the false confidence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: After the match ends a child says he knew that team would lose. The mind quietly rewrites earlier uncertainty into a neat, predictable story.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
